analysis: Two-and-a-half hours after the open, the morning's PCE rally is intact but fading: indexes are off their highs as long-dated yields re-accelerated and oil pushed toward $99. The through-line of the day is that the cooler inflation print gave markets the October-hike reprieve (odds ~35%, from 71% a week ago) while everything else keeps re-pricing against it — strong data (GDP 2.2%, ADP +90K, spending +0.9% m/m) argues for growth, but the 10Y is a few basis points from its 2007 peak and the 30Y mortgage rate just hit a 2.75-year high. The bid remains narrow and momentum-led: software and Mag 7 carry the tape while chips lag (SOXX negative) and the median S&P stock sits 16.7% off its 52-week high — exactly the fragility BofA's AI-put warning is about. Versus the 8am brief: nothing new on the macro data front; the incremental news is the midday fade, the crude-build EIA report, Microsoft's 52-week high, Trump's AI-data-center signal, and Tesla's SEC auto-vote approval. Signal: the 10Y's behavior into the close and Brent near $99. Noise: quarter-end window dressing — today is the last day of Q3.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Stocks trimmed gains heading into midday: long-dated yields climbed again and Brent crude pushed toward $99/bbl, weighing on the early PCE rally. Dow up about 0.1% near 51,419 (off session high 51,473.93), S&P 500 up 0.6%, Nasdaq up 1%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The post-data bid is still alive but fading — rate-relief enthusiasm is running into the yield and oil walls that defined September.

headlines.headline: EIA: US crude stocks rose 922,000 barrels last week (vs a 264,000-barrel draw expected) to 427.3 million barrels; gasoline and distillate inventories fell.
headlines.why_it_matters: Bearish crude-build headline undercuts the morning oil rally, but the product-side draws limit the downside — net neutral for the inflation-via-energy story.

headlines.headline: Treasury choppiness: 10Y around 5.270%, a few basis points from its 2007 peak of 5.303%; 2Y down to ~4.864% after the PCE print. MBA: 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose 18bp to a 2.75-year high of 7.30%; mortgage applications fell 6.0%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Short end cheers the rate-hike reprieve while the long end refuses to — the split keeps financials and housing under pressure even as growth stocks rally.

headlines.headline: Microsoft hit a 52-week high of 519.83, up 1.9% and outperforming the S&P 500, with the relative-strength line at new highs; $3.78T market cap. FY-Q1 consensus: EPS $4.71 (+14%), revenue $90.6B (+17%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Software-side Mag 7 strength is the engine of today's narrow rally — a 52-week high here reinforces the momentum-led tape.

headlines.headline: President Trump reaffirmed support for AI data centers after talks with top AI executives, a fresh political tailwind for the AI buildout trade.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile; if real, it adds policy cover to the AI-capex story ahead of Micron's print, supporting chip sentiment.

headlines.headline: SEC approved Tesla's new voluntary program letting retail shareholders vote automatically with the board; Tesla rose slightly in after-hours. (Cathie Wood's ARK bought ~$17.3M of Tesla and ~$81.6M of Nvidia on Tuesday while selling ~$110M of AMD.)
headlines.why_it_matters: Governance-positive but non-operational — it removes a friction for retail voting, not a catalyst for deliveries or margins. ARK flow is a sentiment read, not a fundamental one.

headlines.headline: Barron's day scorecard: hot stock Carnival +13% (record quarter); biggest loser Fair Isaac -27% after FHFA's Bill Pulte announced mortgage-pricing changes that threaten FICO's credit-score position (largest one-day drop since 1989); best sector utilities +1.1%, worst energy -0.9%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A textbook rotation snapshot: defensive utilities lead while energy lags the crude rally, and the FICO break shows policy risk can still detonate a single name.

headlines.headline: Boeing's F/A-XX Navy win (multi-billion, >$20B per DoD; planes from the 2030s) is Boeing's second sixth-gen fighter program after the F-47; Northrop Grumman fell more than 3% on losing. Mattel named Conde Nast CEO Roger Lynch as its new CEO (-2%); Robinhood unveiled in-app AI agent tools (-premise reversal); Cal-Maine sank ~8% on a wider-than-expected loss.
headlines.why_it_matters: Defense contract news is multi-year revenue visibility for Boeing — slow-burn positive against a stock down 14% YTD; losers' moves are stock-specific, not market-wide.

market_snapshot.breadth_notes: Narrow, momentum-led tape: Mag 7 ETF +1.1% and software ETF +1.3% lead while SOXX -0.2% despite S&P tech +1.3%; only about half of S&P 500 stocks rising; best sector utilities +1.1%, worst energy -0.9%. S&P ~0.4% from all-time peak; median S&P stock 16.7% below its 52-week closing high (Barron's). No sourced advance/decline ratio or volume-vs-average data.
market_snapshot.notes: Wednesday ~2.5h after open (midday ET): Dow +0.1% (~51,419, off high 51,473.93), S&P 500 +0.6%, Nasdaq +1% — fading from best levels as long-dated yields re-climb and Brent nears $99 (MarketWatch). Tuesday close: Dow -0.26% (51,349.92), S&P 500 -0.17% (7,670.84), Nasdaq -0.09% (26,797.54).

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning. Carried forward: Wall Street Zen downgraded USAC from buy to hold (Sep 26); the stock broke below its 200-day MA ($27.12, traded as low as $25.25) on Friday. Final NYSE trading day is Friday Oct 2; units begin trading on the Texas Stock Exchange on Oct 5 under the unchanged ticker.

watch_next: Micron earnings after the close — revenue expected ~$50.95-51.3B (+~350%), EPS ~$31.63-31.72; options imply ~9% move; AI-memory commentary and guidance matter most for the chip complex.
Remaining Fed speakers today (Kashkari and others) — any October-hike signal moves yields and growth multiples.
Friday: September jobs report (NFP +90K expected, unemployment 4.1%) — the week's main event for the Fed-hike debate.
USAC: final NYSE trading day Friday Oct 2; units begin trading on the Texas Stock Exchange on Oct 5 (ticker unchanged).
